assays.assay_name: Open Field Air-Puff Threat Responding (locomotor) Assay
assays.assay_description: Rats freely explored a 50 x 50 cm clear plexiglass open field within a sound-dampened cabinet. Each session comprised a 10-min habituation/baseline period followed by two 500-ms, 85-psi air-puffs delivered to the face with a 5-min inter-stimulus interval. Behaviour (distance travelled, max speed, % time in centre, time immobile; active vs. passive threat-responding classification) was recorded with ANY-maze at 1-min and 1-s resolution. Sessions were run at baseline, on the day of vehicle/psilocin injection (30 min post-dose), and at 2- and 14-day follow-ups, in male and female rats across the standard PVT GCaMP and intersectional PVT→CeA cohorts (fiber photometry recorded concurrently but not scored).

application_type.evidence: animals received subcutaneous (s.c.) injections of either vehicle (2% glacial acetic acid in 0.9% saline) or psilocin (2 mg/kg)

setup_habituation.evidence: On the day of recording, animals were habituated to the room for 1 hr after which they were placed in chambers for 10min habituation and baseline recording; prior to the air-puff session animals received '10 min habituation' in the open field box.

setup_restrain.evidence: Locomotor activity was assessed in a clear, plexiglass open field apparatus (50 cm×50 cm); animals moved freely and no restraint is described.

food_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to food and water in the home cage; no food was present in the open field apparatus during recording.

water_restriction.evidence: ad libitum access to food and water in the home cage; no water was present in the open field apparatus during recording.

time_to_assay.evidence: animals were given an injection of either vehicle or psilocin (2mg/kg, s.c.) and placed in home cage for 20 min prior to 10 min habituation for a total of 30 min prior to the beginning of the air-puff session. Follow-up recordings were collected at 2- and 14-days post administration.

sample_size.evidence: Fig. 2 (female PVT): Vehicle: n = 8; Psilocin: n=6. Fig. 6 (female PVT→CeA): Vehicle: n = 11; Psilocin: n=11. Fig. 8 (male PVT→CeA): Vehicle: n=7; Psilocin: n=6. Fig. 9: Passive Psilocin: n=2.

outcomes.summary: Behaviourally, acute psilocin (2 mg/kg, s.c.) reduced the proportion of females displaying an active (escape/darting) response to the air-puff on the day of injection, and was associated with decreased maximum speed and increased time immobile after the air-puff in the female PVT cohort. These behavioural effects were not present at the 2- and 14-day follow-ups, and males showed no comparable psilocin-induced changes (with scattered subgroup effects on max speed and immobility).
outcomes.statistics: Fisher's exact test: p=0.0256 (active responding, day of injection, vehicle vs psilocin). Max speed: 2-way ANOVA Finteraction(9,117)=5.212, p<0.0001; Finjection(1,13)=5.181, p=0.0404. Time immobile: Finteraction(9,117)=2.377, p=0.0166; Finjection(1,13)=1.832, p=0.1989. Psilocin active responders max speed: Finteraction(9,63)=7.357, p<0.0001; Fsession(1,7)=6.749, p=0.0355. Female PVT→CeA passive responders at injection: max speed Ftreatment(1,7)=8.270, p=0.0238; time immobile Ftreatment(1,7)=6.034, p=0.0437.
outcomes.evidence: On the day of injection, active responding was reduced in psilocin treated animals (Fig. 3C), with a significant difference between vehicle and psilocin treated groups (Fisher's exact test: p=0.0256). The increase in PVT reactivity was associated with a decrease in max speed ... and an increase in time immobile in the first 3 seconds following air-puff.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Measures of locomotor activity included distance traveled (m), max speed (m/s), % time spent in the center zone, and time immobile; animals were additionally classified as active vs. passive responders.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Analysis across time were calculated at 1 min resolution for the overall locomotor behaviors, and additionally at 1 s for the immediate post puff behavioral analysis to correspond with fiber photometry time points.

B4_ethological.evidence: Active responders were defined as animals that employed evasive locomotor behavior in response to the air-puff and actively moved away from the quadrant where the air-puff occurred... passive responders were defined as rats that did not display enhanced locomotor behavior or actively try to escape the air-puff.

B5_social.evidence: Animals were tested individually in the open field; no social construct or conspecific involved.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Air-puff reactivity is an innate defensive/threat response; no learning or memory requirement is described.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Behavioral sessions were recorded and analyzed with ANY-maze video tracking system (Stoelting Co, IL, USA).

B8_multivariate.evidence: All data were graphed and statistically analyzed with Prism 10.0.3; only univariate t-tests and ANOVAs reported.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Locomotor activity was assessed in a clear, plexiglass open field apparatus (50 cm×50 cm) which was located within a sound dampened activity cabinet.

E2_shelter.evidence: Open field apparatus with no enclosed refuge; definitionally absent.

E3_bedding.evidence: Clear plexiglass open field apparatus; no bedding reported in the testing chamber.

E4_nesting.evidence: Nestlet enrichment was in the home cage only; no nesting material described in the open field.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects described in the open field apparatus during recording.

E6_spatial.evidence: Open field apparatus (50 cm×50 cm) with a virtual centre zone defined within the tracking software; no physical compartments.

E7_social_context.evidence: Focal rat was placed alone into the open field box; no conspecific present during recording.

E8_food_water.evidence: Ad libitum food and water were available in the home cage only; none in the open field during recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: Baseline recordings were used to demonstrate changes... prior to drug administration. Followup recordings were collected at 2- and 14-days post administration.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each session consisted of a 10min habituation baseline period before the delivery of two air-puff administrations with a 5min inter-stimulus interval (ISI); behavioural measurements were collected within the 10-min habituation and the 5-min ISI (≥15 min total).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Timeline: BL, 0d (day of injection), 2d, 14d — four distinct recording days for this assay.

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline recordings were used to demonstrate changes in fluorescence (ΔF/F) prior to drug administration; baseline behavioural responding was used to classify active vs. passive responders.

D5_followup.evidence: Followup recordings were collected at 2- and 14-days post administration.

D6_circadian.evidence: Sessions lasted ~15 min; no recording spanned ≥6 hours.

judge_notes: All three candidates identified a single behavioural paradigm (open field + air-puff); these were merged into one assay entry ('Open Field Air-Puff Threat Responding'). Candidate names differed ('Open Field Test (with air-puff stimulus)', 'Aversive Air-Puff Response') but describe the same apparatus/protocol.

Fiber photometry (GCaMP calcium signals), c-Fos immunohistochemistry and retrograde tracing were excluded per the rubric (neural recordings / histology are not behavioural assays). Only the locomotor/threat-responding behaviour measured with ANY-maze was scored.

Male and female cohorts, standard-GCaMP vs. intersectional PVT→CeA cohorts, active vs. passive responder splits, and the BL/0d/2d/14d timepoints were collapsed into one assay per the rubric's assay-identity rules.

B1 scored 2 (4-6): the Methods explicitly list four locomotor measures (distance travelled, max speed, % centre time, time immobile), overriding candidates that counted only the two measures shown in figures.

B4 scored 1 (Yes): active/passive threat-responding (evasive darting/escape vs. freezing) is a directly scored natural defensive behaviour, not merely locomotor distance; two of three candidates missed this.

D2 scored 1 (15-60 min): the session comprises a 10-min habituation baseline plus two air-puffs separated by a 5-min ISI, with behaviour analysed in both windows, totalling ≥15 min; this overrides gemma4's <15 min.
D3 scored 1 (2-7 days): four recording days (BL, injection, 2d, 14d) — gemma4's score of 2 was inconsistent with its own '2-7' category label.
setup_habituation = yes: a 1-h room acclimation plus a 10-min in-chamber habituation is described; the in-chamber habituation also overlaps with baseline recording, so confidence set to medium.
